utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Thank you, Madam Registrar. I see that according to the transcript, today, Monday, the 18th of April, the accused entered court -- oh, the accused. Sorry, I was thinking the witness. Okay. Thank you. Yes, may we have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Joanna Korner, Alex Demirdjian, and Crispian Smith for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic, Slobodan Cvijetic, Eugene O'Sullivan, and Ms. Tatjana Savic appearing for the Stanisic Defence this morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Dragan Krgovic and Aleksandar Aleksic appearing for Zupljanin Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, we gather that the OTP has something to raise before the witness resumes the -- his testimony.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Two short matters, Your Honour. First is this. Going back, I had a gripping Sunday reading through the transcripts of last week, and I noticed on Thursday, the 14th of April, the transcript seems to have a number of errors. But the most important which I feel I ought to correct because it could have a knock-on effect. This is during the course of the legal argument when I was putting forward the Office of the Prosecutor's view. We were discussing -- or I was discussing, I'm sorry, at page 19576, the various documents that we had received from Mr. Bjelosevic. And at page 19577, line 3, I'm recorded as saying: "After the --" well, at line 1. "After the to-ing and fro-ing over then-Colonel now General Lisic's documents and his book, and all the" apparently indiscernible, "and we accept entirely buried in our vaults," I'm now then recorded as saying, "Mr. Milosevic had, in fact, given us way back in 2004 ..." I did, of course, say Mr. Bjelosevic. I appreciate the names sound the same. But it seems to me that is an error that should be corrected. Your Honours, secondly, for the second matter, can I go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just on the page 1, line 16, Mr. Cvijetic was not recorded as present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Would the Usher please escort the witness back to the stand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Good morning to you, sir. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And, as usual, before Mr. Zecevic continues, I remind you of your solemn declaration which you're still under. Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Bjelosevic.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, could you please briefly explain to all of us the procedure that was undertaken by the police in keeping with the Law on Internal Affairs and regulations that regulated those issues, in case information was received that an incident had taken place?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Upon receipt of such a report, firstly, the person who received the report, usually it was the duty police officer, entered the most essential data and then informed the duty officer. Usually it was the duty operations officer, or, if the -- that was in the police station, that would be the duty operations policeman. And in line with the incident, and I'm speaking hypothetically, either it was a traffic accident, or a disruption of public law and order, or a crime, the most immediate patrol was sent to secure the area. Again, depending on the type of crime, a team was established to carry out an on-site investigation. If we're talking about the period of 1992, an investigating judge and the prosecutor would be informed if the crime was of such a nature that it was mandatory. And that was done in -- in cases of murder, in cases of injuries or more substantial material damage.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, at what point you, and when you [as interpreted] say "you" I mean the police, at what point could you establish that a crime was committed in a certain case?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The initial information that was received was checked from its very source. And then the qualified information was established when the police was sent to the site of the incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bjelosevic, in the course of 1992, from the moment when the Security Services Centre was reinstated and became operational again, did you file criminal reports against perpetrators of crime in your Security Services Centre?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From the moment when the centre established its sections and departments and when it started functioning along the lines of work, I believe that everything functioned according to regulations, starting with on-site investigations, creating documentation, i.e., opening a case as an investigation case, informing investigative judges and prosecutors, recording everything that was pertinent to the case. Reports were filed both for unknown and known perpetrators. When the perpetrator was not known, we continued to work towards elucidating the crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, was a distinction made in terms of the ethnicity of victims as opposed to the ethnicity of perpetrators?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Those distinctions were never made. There were incidents in our areas in which members of different ethnic groups were both victims and perpetrators of certain crimes, and our approach was the same in all those cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the Usher please assist us and provide Mr. Bjelosevic with this binder with documents. Could the witness please be shown 1D356, tab 76. 1D356, tab 76.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, this is a criminal report by the Security Services Centre in Doboj. The date is the 1st of August, 1992. Your name is typed up. There is also a signature. Could you please tell us whether you're familiar with this document; and can you also explain things about this document, especially in the right-hand side corner we see handwritten "additions." Could you please explain that as well.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a criminal report against unknown perpetrators of the crime of murder. Article 36 is quoted and so on and so forth. The victim was Sejfudin Hadzimujic. You can tell by the name that the person, the victim, was a Muslim. The crime was committed on the 23rd of July. There's a short description of the crime. There's also evidence that is enclosed together with a criminal report, and the Official Note that was drafted on the scene and photo documentation which means that an on-site investigation had been carried out. At the handwritten notes or additions, depict the word "records" and there is a signature of Veljko Solaja, and there is also a log-book number KU 5/92, which means that under that -- this number the whole file was recorded in the centre. As you can see, the investigating judge had been informed about the incident. He had ordered that an autopsy be performed in the pathology department. You -- and you can see from this criminal report what the entire procedure looked like.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us who Veljko Solaja is?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Veljko Solaja was an inspector who worked at the Security Services Centre at the time. He was affiliated with the crime department, and he was specialised in homicides.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown 1D357. 357. Tab 77.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is another criminal report. It bears the same date, the 1st of August, 1992. On the second page, you will see the typed up signature. There's are some additions here as well in the upper right-hand side corner. Can you please confirm whether this criminal report was filed by the Security Services Centre in Doboj; and can you please explain the handwritten additions in the right-hand side corner?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is also a document that was drafted at the Doboj Security Services Centre. Can you see the number and the date. I signed this criminal report. I signed this document. From the document, you can see that the crime was allegedly committed. There are suspicions that a crime was committed on the 17 July 1992, and that alleged crime was committed at the Begovic house at Petko Djuric Street and so on and so forth. What follows is a description of the crime where it says that most probably at around 2230 hours on 17 July 1992, an unknown perpetrator entered the Begovic house and that he committed the aforementioned crime. Again, the persons involved in the crime were Muslims. The procedure was the same. An investigating judge was informed and then, at the end, you can see the evidence that was attached with the criminal report; the Official Note about the interview carried out with Emir Begovic, Sabina Savic and Jusuf Savic [as interpreted]; photo documentation of the on-site investigation. And as you can see, in this case again, the bodies of the victims had been sent for autopsy.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: There's no need to go in so much detail because we can all see it in the criminal report. I would like to hear your comment of the handwritten additions. Can you please tell us who did that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you can see, this was recorded and it says that this copy is for the records, and the signature is that of Branislav Petricevic, who at the time was an inspector in the crime department of the Security Services Centre in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D362, tab 80, is the next document I would like to call up.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is a criminal report dated the 3rd of August. On the second page, you will see that your name is typed up. There's also your signature. The document was drafted at the Doboj Security Services Centre. This criminal report is against known perpetrators. Could you please briefly tell us whether you remember this incident, whether that criminal report was, indeed, drafted at your CSB. And again, in the right-hand side corner, we see a handwritten entry.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is, indeed, a document which was drafted at the Security Services Centre. The document bears my signature. This is a criminal report against known perpetrators, Vukasin Vukojevic and Mirko Ninkovic. The crime in question, as described in this criminal report, is murder, and the victims were Muslims and Croats. All right. In the right-hand side upper corner, again, there's a note that the criminal report has to be filed in the records and the signature is that of Veljko Solaja.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at 1D355, tab 246.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is also a criminal report. The date is the same. On page 2, we can see Chief of Centre, Andrija Bjelosevic, as well as your signature. And, again, in the upper right corner, we see some handwriting. Can you confirm that this is also a criminal report from your centre, that you signed it, and could you explain what it is.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document originated from the Security Services Centre. It bears my signature. It's a criminal report against Zoran Ninkovic. It relates to an act that was committed in the way that is described here on the 31st of July, and the criminal report dates from the 3rd of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Is this criminal report related to the previous one?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As you can see, the victim is Ivan Cigoj. He was listed as the victim in the previous report. And we can see that the further investigative work yielded new information. New facts were discovered which means that the criminal report was then expanded to include this person as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The following document is 205D1, tab 83. Can we have the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This document is dated 5th of August, 1992. It also contains typed words "Chief of Centre, Andrija Bjelosevic." Can you confirm that this is your document, and can you explain it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a document originating from the Security Services Centre in Doboj and it bears my signature. I remember this. This is a memo drafted by the policemen of the public security station in Maglaj that was headquartered in Jablanica. It's a memo about the conduct of a certain soldier. Since this was a person from the jurisdiction of the military organs, we forwarded this memo to the military security organ in the command of the operations group of Doboj, because they were supposed to act on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there is no objection, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D480, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document is 379D1, tab 87.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Is it a document originating in the Doboj Security Services Centre, dated the 10th of August, 1992, and does it bear your signature?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was sent to the public prosecutor's office. And you can see that there is an enclosure and that was the Official Note drafted on site where the fire broke out. And you can also see up there, "Records, Veljko Solaja, inspector."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, could you explain why in this case this is an Official Note; and what is the difference between Official Notes and criminal reports?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: An Official Note is a document containing descriptions of information of things that were found, and, as such, this document is the basis for further work. The information contained therein is then used for further action. This document was sent to the public prosecutor's office, and then it was that office that made the decision about what ought to be done. As far as I can remember, they requested the police, which, at the time was called milicija, to gather some supplemental information related to this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What kind of supplemental information? Can you explain that.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember what it was in this specific case, but it was the usual procedure. When the prosecutor begins his work, he can request supplemental information about what he thinks is necessary for his work.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right. You do remember something about this. Do you know what was the ethnicity of the victim?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jozo Barukcic is a Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there is no objection, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Are the enclosure and attachments part of this document, Mr. Zecevic? It refers to and attached Official Note, "We enclose an Official Note ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, we don't have the Official Note, Your Honours. We just have this -- this document as -- as a cover sheet sent to the Office of the Prosecutor in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So the -- we've heard the witness's testimony. How does this piece of paper assist further beyond what the witness has said?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, one of the issues in this case --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you take off your headphones, Mr. Bjelosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: One of the issues in this case, Your Honours, is the theory and the position of the Office of the Prosecutor that there was a certain different approach of the -- of the police in 1992 in case where the -- where the perpetrators are Serbs or unknown perpetrators, and the victims are -- are of -- are non-Serbs. Now, in this case, this unfortunate person lost his life in the arsony or maybe it was -- maybe it wasn't the arsony, but just the fire that caught his house. Now, I would like to -- I would like to tender this document for two reasons. One, because the witness explained what the Official Note is, and I believe we have seen and we will see a number of these documents in the future; and the second, I think it's relevant because it shows that the police was conducting proper investigations in cases where the victims were non-Serbs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I think I follow all of that, Mr. Zecevic. And if the relevant enclosures were there, it would make perfect sense. My only question is whether without that, whether we need this additional piece of paper. Nothing much turns on it. It is just a question of reducing in some small way the bulk of paper which comprise the exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honours. But, unfortunately, we don't have the attachment to this document. And this document on the -- in this document, we see all the relevant issues that I -- that I was just talking about. That is why I was offering it for -- to be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, is the -- can you question the witness further on this to see what -- whether he could assist us in terms of what was conveyed in this cover note?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I understand. I will, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I'm relying on the fact that this is his -- that he signed this one. So presumably he should -- so please pursue it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bjelosevic, did you sign this document? Do you know this document?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know the document. This is my signature. And now, having read it, I remember the event in question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Since this is the first, or the covering page of the document, and we do not have this attachment, could you maybe try to cast your mind back as much as you could and tell us what it was in this attachment in the Official Note?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's been a long time ago, and I really don't remember the contents.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you maybe remember what instructions you received from the prosecutor's office, what additional information they requested?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that they requested some further details that were supposed to supplement the eye-witness statements, but I do not remember the contents. I really don't remember that. I remember this case, and I remember that we worked on it at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether a criminal report was finally submitted in this case or not?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, perhaps I'll ask the witness. Mr. Witness, can you explain, give the reason, probably the obvious reason, why this is an Official Note and not a criminal report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't receive the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Bjelosevic, could you explain why, the reason, probably the obvious reason, why this is an Official Note and not a criminal report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't get the interpretation. I can hear now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Can you hear it now? Okay. So the question is: Can you explain, can you give the -- probably the obvious reason, the reason why this is an Official Note and not a criminal report.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I can remember this case, when the policemen went on the site, it was established that the fire was an accident. That was the first information. Now, as to what happened later on, I really am not in the position to claim anything. I think that the prosecutor requested additional information. Now, whether it was -- it remained classified as an accident or whether it was reclassified as an arson, I'm afraid that I'm going to make a mistake if I say anything about it because I don't remember the details. I think that certain misunderstandings between the victim and his wife were also involved in this case, but I really don't remember the details.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, I think you've taken it as far as you could, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honours. [Interpretation] P1340, tab 90.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, take a look at this document. It contains a covering letter and a further two pages of a report. And when you see the whole document, I'm going to ask you a question. Do you remember having received this document in August 1992?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. And although it is not stated here, this document was compiled at my request because, at the time, there were quite a few automobiles that were driven around by members of the army and even the members of the milicija, and without proper documents at that. So perhaps one could say that they were doing that illegally. If I remember correctly, I wasn't actually satisfied with this document. If I remember correctly, we actually had a discussion about this. Because I asked for a specific reference to be made to the motor vehicles that were available to the milicija, and I asked for the origin of these vehicles to be stated. In listing these vehicles, as far as I can remember, the members of the police from Banja Luka who are referred to here, indeed, had taken a VAU [as interpreted] vehicle, as far as can I remember. It wasn't a Passat, it was a Jetta. We asked for further checks with regard to the matter and I don't know how all this was brought to an end. This is a Renault 5 that is being referred to here. It is a vehicle that was at the basic court in Doboj, as far as I can remember. And I know that, after that, there were proceedings instituted against Slobodan Karagic, from Doboj, with regard to that vehicle. And so on and so forth. Not to go into each and every detail, but at the time, in that chaos, as it was, that is something that did happen. Namely, that vehicles were being seized from their owners and that what they would say was that the vehicle had been mobilised. However, agreement between the owner of the vehicle and the person who took the vehicle away from the owner, that is one thing. However, that cannot be considered mobilisation. Mobilisation meant that a vehicle would be taken and registered at the Department for National Defence, that the owner be issued a certificate to that effect, and when a vehicle is mobilised, then the owner receives a proper certificate with which he can obtain compensation if the vehicle is destroyed or damaged. I insisted on that. I insisted that things be done that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bjelosevic. Could you please have a look at document 1D361, tab 97. This is a criminal report dated the 24th of August. It has a signature and a stamp. It is provided to the public prosecutor's office. Could you please tell us whose document this is; are you familiar with the document; and can you explain to us the handwritten portion at the top of the page?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document is of the CSB Doboj, and I recognise this document. I signed it. My signature is at the end of the document. As for the handwritten part, it has to do with records yet again. I cannot recognise the signature now that is underneath the other handwritten word, but it must be one of the inspectors.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document is 380D1, tab 99.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I remember this document. It's a document from the Security Services Centre of Doboj. And the date is there, and my signature is at the end of the document. Perhaps I should explain this in a bit more detail. In the area of Svjetlica, that is a settlement that dominates over the town, as it were, it's on the right bank of the Bosna river, there was unit there, a JNA unit, that was established sometime in the beginning of 1992, I believe. I think that it only consisted of ethnic Muslims. The commander of the unit was Durmic Mirsad, if I remember correctly. That unit stayed on there. They practically held that area under their control. It was not involved at the front line any further. I think that when this particular incident occurred, Major Stankovic and these other persons had set out to see this man called Durmic, to have a meeting with him. Then they came across a land-mine, and the consequences are described here. It was a bit of a surprise, how come there were mines there if the unit was part of the army, and if the agreement had been for them to come there that way. But, anyway, that is the incident that is involved here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, in this case as well, was an Official Note compiled, or were certain proceedings instituted, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From our side - and when I say "our side," I mean the police - only an Official Note was compiled. I'm not aware of what the military organs actually did. I'm not aware of any details.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, you said to us last week when we were talking about the shelling of Doboj -- actually, was this treated as a crime; and, if so, which crime?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was treated as a crime. It was treated as a crime against the civilian population at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Were criminal reports filed?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: During 1992, what about the use of shells and other explosive devices? How was that treated? Was it treated as a crime; and, if so, which crime?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if we're talking about the use of artillery against the town, then that is a crime. It is a crime against the civilian population. Obviously that was the case here, in this case that you are discussing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And when hand-grenades are used and explosive devices that can also be hand held, when such explosive devices were thrown, if I can put it that way, was that treated as a crime; and, if so, which crime?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was treated as the crime of causing general danger for the public. And, now, if there were consequences, then that depended, whether the result was death or not. But, anyway, it was treated as causing general danger.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Were criminal reports filed for the commission of such crimes?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please look at 381D1, tab 122.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is a criminal report submitted to the higher public prosecutor's office in Doboj, the CSB. It has a signature and a stamp. Could you please tell us whether you're familiar with the document. Can you tell us who signed it; can you tell us more about it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document of the Doboj CSB. It was signed by the chief of the public security sector, Mirko Stojcinovic. This is, indeed, his signature; I can recognise it. I also remember the incident itself, and you can see in the upper right-hand corner what was added was "operative records," and underneath that, the number 16/92, as the number of the register.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If you remember the incident itself, or, on the basis of this criminal report, can you tell us who the injured parties were in this incident?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there is no objection, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D481, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document, 382D1, tab 128.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this document is also a criminal report. The date is the 22nd of September, 1992. Your name is typewritten, as well as your title. There is no signature. There is no stamp. And there is something that is handwritten on the top of the document. Tell me, are you familiar with the document; and could you please explain what it was that is written here.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The document is from the Security Services Centre. You can see the number of the register there on the top of the page. It is a criminal report against perpetrators unknown. It has to do with a crime committed against Smail Jukic, who is an ethnic Muslim. In the upper right-hand corner, again, it says "operative records." This means that this is a copy for those records, and then there's a signature there and a number, 18/92.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there is no objection, I would like to tender this document into evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D482, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document is 217D1, tab 110.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this document is dated the 10th of September, 1992. Your name and surname are typed out at the end of the page. It also says "chief." Do you remember the document; and can you tell us more about this? First of all, is it your document from the CSB Doboj and who was it sent to?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The document is from the CSB. It is a dispatch, and you can see that it has to do with a crime that was committed when a military unit passed through a certain area. They were going out to carry out a combat task somewhere. And, in this case, it is Serbs who are the injured party, this woman whose name was Draginja, and you can also see the buildings that were fired at. There were such incidents, generally speaking. That is to say, that the perpetrators of these crimes did not really mind who this was aimed against. This kind of thing did happen. I would like to say, once again, that this area, the area of Doboj, and this is a settlement that belongings to the Doboj municipality, was in total chaos all the time, inter alia, because of the presence of these military units that took turns there at the front line and also because of a large number of refugees and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether in this particular case a criminal report was filed?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was within the purview of military bodies, and you can see that this is just information and that several crimes or several incidents, rather, are listed in here. This was meant to be included in the MUP information bulletin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unless there are objections, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I mean, I haven't objected so far, but at the moment I'm not clear to what issue this is going. It's not a report -- or it's a report to the MUP. Doesn't appear to be an investigation. Nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I believe the witness explained and -- and this is the report which -- which the witness said it was sent to the MUP for the purposes of daily bulletin of the MUP of RS.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, well, I don't think we're raising any issue about whether Mr. Bjelosevic, at this stage, was reporting to his superiors. In fact, the contrary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, do I correctly assume, as was the case with a number of items last week, that this is in the category of illustrations. And assuming that to be the position, the -- there would -- of necessity have to be a limited number of these because there's an a point at which the utility is -- they have no utility, no practical utility.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I must say that you -- you scare me, Your Honours, when you say that that doesn't have a practical utility. If --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... merely illustrative.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps the witness should remove his earphones. Your Honours, one of the issues in this case is the notice of the MUP of RS on the events that were happening in the field. And, I agree this -- this particular document is illustrative about that. However, it is illustrative about the overall situation again, and that is the purpose why I offer this document. But the previous documents, the criminal reports which I entered into the evidence, you will remember that two days -- on Thursday, we had a long discussion with Ms. Korner about the KU register, and, therefore --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: If I might interrupt, the criminal report's in a different category. They --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, it was my misunderstanding, then. That's why I said that I was scared when you say there's no practical utility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: But this appears to be a report of an incident which, on the face of it, isn't criminal. And it is -- when I talk about being merely illustrative, it is that category of documents to which -- in respect of which we have reservations about how many of these we need.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But, Your Honours, with all due respect, I must disagree with you. This is definitely a criminal -- this is a criminal case. But what the witness said was that it wasn't within their authority. It was the authority of the army, and -- and that is why he -- he didn't took any measures because the -- the persons who committed this are obviously the members of the military unit, both or all three events which happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we'll admit it. Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D483, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the last document before the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Put on the microphones and put the headphones back on. Are you receiving interpretation?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 228D1, tab 125, is the last document I would like to call up before the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, could you please look at the second page. Do you remember this document? Is this your document? It is dated the 19th of September, 1992. Could you just briefly tell us what the document is about.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is, indeed, a document issued by the Security Services Centre. I can't give you the protocol number. The document bears my signature. And this is an Official Note which was attached to the cover letter, and it was sent to the Osinje Brigade command. I believe we have already mentioned this brigade before during my testimony. In the left-hand side corner, you have a note which says that this is a copy which was archived. And if I'm not mistaken, this is Mirko Blazanovic's signature. I'm not sure, but I believe that the signature is indeed his. And the subject is the conduct of the brigade's troops. We inform the command, asking them to take measures within their purview, because those soldiers were under their authority, and they were duty-bound to take measures in such cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Was that a customary way you acted in cases when army troops were involved in breaches of discipline or crimes? How did you report to the army about the conduct of their members?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was a customary manner we did it. At the time, I would like to say the troops were under the authority of military prosecutor's offices, military judges, or the command. The command had a right to institute certain measures in case of minor breaches, and we were duty-bound to inform them about any incidents that involved members of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document into evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D484, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps -- because I have another document, but I -- I'm -- I might try to show it to the witness just to use up the time. [Interpretation] 383D1 is the following document, at tab 147.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, please look at the document and tell us whether it was drafted by yourself. What can you tell us about this document? Again, in the right-hand side corner, we see handwritten additions, and I would like to seek your explanation of those as well.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document was issued by the Security Services Centre in Doboj. It's a criminal report against a person whose name was Andro Deronja, who committed the crime of murder. He killed his wife. The typed-up name is my name, and I signed the document. And in the right-hand side corner, this is an added handwritten note, which says that this should be filed in the records. The person who signed that is Veljko Solaja, whom we already mentioned. He was an inspector in the crime department.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you help us with the ethnic background of the victim?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that both were Croats, both the perpetrator and the victim. I'm not sure, but I would think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D485, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I must comment that in terms of the translated document, in the second paragraph, I assume that the concept was that she had died instantly, not momentarily. So we take the break and resume in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: May I continue, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bjelosevic, the following document I would like to look at is 384D1, tab 148. This is a criminal report dated 19 October 1992. Let's just wait for the English translation to appear before we continue. Your name is typed up at the bottom of the document. There's also a signature. Could you please explain the nature of this document? Did you sign it? Are you familiar with the document?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document was issued by the Security Services Centre of Doboj. It is a criminal report against unknown perpetrators. The victim of the crime was Zulfo Ciric. He was a Muslim. My name is indeed typed up, but on my behalf the document was signed by Mirko Stojcinovic, who was the chief of the public security sector. In the right-hand side upper corner, there's a number of the log-book and it also says that the file -- the report has to be filed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unless there are objections, I would like to tender that document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, could we inquire from the witness if he can tell us about the ethnicity of the victim.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I believe the witness said, line 29 [sic], line 7, he was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Sorry, I see that now. That's very good. Thank you. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D486, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The following document is 239D1, tab 150.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is a document issued by the Security Services Centre in Doboj. The date is 22nd October 1992. It has a signature and a stamp. Could you please tell us whether this is your document? Are you familiar with the document? And what is the document about?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the document originating in the Security Services Centre in Doboj. It was addressed to the Ministry of the Interior; specifically to the crime prevention administration. I signed the document. This is a covering letter that also -- that accompanied the decision and the order from the military court in Bijeljina, which, in 1992, had jurisdiction over Doboj. They requested the issuance of a search circular for the persons listed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Was this the usual practice at the time, that was observed at the time?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the usual practice. If a military court requested issuance of search circulars pertaining to certain persons, this would normally be forwarded to this administration, and then the Ministry of the Interior would issue a search circular through its central register. Or, sometimes, it would be search pertaining to property.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, we can see in this document that it mentions an order originating from a military court. Did the Ministry of the Interior, or more specifically, the Security Services Centre, were they also in a position to request a search to be performed; and, if so, how did they do that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If a need arose and there were such situations, centres and stations could also request a search. They would follow the same procedure, and a search circular would be issued, listing the names of the persons that had to be found.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Would you inform the Ministry of the Interior and its crime prevention administration also in those cases?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the normal procedure. That's how it was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D487, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, so sorry, Your Honours, could I just have the tab number again.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The previous document. 150.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The one that is on the screen, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: 150. [Interpretation] I would now like to take a look at tab 162. It's 251D1.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, this document is, again, a document originating from the Security Services Centre. The date is the 6th of November, 1992. It was sent to the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska to the Crime Prevention and Detection Administration. On the second page, we can see your name typed, and I would like you to tell us whether this is your document, whether you are familiar with its contents, and also, again, on the first page, we see some handwritten remarks, and I would like to hear your comments on them. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a document originating from the Security Services Centre in Doboj. It was addressed to the Ministry of the Interior, as you said, to the Crime Prevention and Detection Administration. It is about searching for property that has been alienated from the territory of the Zavidovici municipality. I signed this document. In the upper right corner, we can see handwritten something that relates to Petricevic, that is Branislav Petricevic, Inspector. He belonged to the Crime Prevention Department. This is a recommendation by his boss, which says: "Monitor activities in connection with this request." And we can see the signature of the Crime Prevention Department, Vojo Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there is no objection, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D488.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, we don't have the number in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D488. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like to take a look at 391D1, tab 164A.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you please take a look at this document, sir. It comes from the public security station in Teslic. The date is the 9th of November, 1992. Are you familiar with this document; and can you comment on it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, the public security station Teslic functioned within the Security Services Centre in Banja Luka. I did not have a chance to see this document at the time, but I can see the signature, and that is the signature of Radomir Jokic, the chief of the station. I also see the log number at the top, and I assume that this is a document originating from the public security station in Teslic, because this man was the chief of that station at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you see in this document who was the victim? More precisely, what was the ethnicity of the victim and what was the ethnicity of the perpetrator?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by the names, the perpetrators are obviously Serbs. Hasan Kahrimanovic, the injured party, is obviously a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And what is the criminal offence alleged?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Arson, which is a crime against property.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there is no objection, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D489, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The following document is 385D1, tab 194.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, this is a document coming from the Security Services Centre in Doboj on the 3rd of December, 1992. It's a criminal report submitted to the public prosecutor's office. We can see your name typed in the signature block, and we can also see your signature. Could you comment on this document? Did you sign it? Is it your document? And what is it about?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This document comes from the Security Services Centre in Doboj. It's a criminal report against an unidentified perpetrator because there are reasonable grounds to suspect that he had committed the crime of murder against Latif Suljkic from Doboj. Latif Suljkic was a Muslim. As you can see, attached are the documents that could be considered evidence. They pertain to the interviews carried out with Sefik Suljkic and Mihreta Terzic; they're also Muslims. I signed this document. In the upper right-hand corner, you can see that it says "Records," then there is the KU number, and that number is 31/92.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there is no objection, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D490.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, could I ask you how many further documents do you wish to have admitted to show that there was reporting from the CSB in Doboj about crimes to the public prosecutor in Doboj? Perhaps if you have a lot of them, we could group them all together and have them admitted in one batch, rather than having to go through --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I mean --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: They seem to be very similar these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they are criminal complaints filed by the CSB Doboj to the public -- the district attorney in Doboj, and those are the documents where the victims were non-Serbs. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: How many more --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I have two more. But I'm in the hands of Your Honours. I can offer them ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes, let me consult with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, let's have the two documents now. But if, in the rest of the documents that you wish to tender, you have documents that could be batched together and admitted in one go, I think that would save time and energy for all of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honours. [Interpretation] The next document is 386D1, tab 210.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, this is a document from the Security Services Centre in Doboj, dated the 23rd of December, 1992. Your name is typed at the bottom under "Chief of Centre." There is no signature, however. Can you confirm that this is your document, and do you maybe remember anything else about it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a document from the Security Services Centre in Doboj. It was addressed to the public prosecutor's office in Doboj. It's also a criminal report against an unidentified perpetrator against Hasib Alicehajic and Muharem Alicehajic. They are Muslims who were living in Doboj. Attached to this document are also the Official Note and photo documentation from the site. And in the upper right-hand corner, we can see additional note that it was sent to the records, and the KU number is 34/92.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there is no objection, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D491, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next document is 387D1, tab 212. We have the document now. Let us just wait for the translation as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is a criminal report as well, signed by Chief of Centre, Andrija Bjelosevic. The date is the 28th of December, 1992. Tell me, can you recognise the document? Is it your document? What can you tell us about it.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is a document of the CSB Doboj. I signed it. It involves the crime of causing general danger. An unknown perpetrator placed an explosive device at the door of the premises of Glas Komuna; that was a regional newspaper company. You can see that some documents here are attached that can be used as evidence; Official Notes, photographic documentation, et cetera. Again, in the upper right-hand corner, it says "evidencije," records. However, you cannot see the number because when photocopying the document, something was placed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there are no objections, I would like to tender this document as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D492, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, let us look at document 389D1, tab 215. Sir, tell us whether you're familiar with this document; and, if so, could you please explain it to us. Tell us what it is about.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document that is an excerpt from the register of the CSB Doboj. Criminal reports are registered in that document against certain perpetrators. Brief information is provided as to who the injured parties were and who criminal reports were filed against. There are also some brief remarks with regard to the status of the case file -- or, rather, further measures that were being taken and so on. So this is an extract from that register. I think that some of the criminal reports that are referred to here were the ones that we looked at.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On page 2, we can see numbers up to 11, and then there is an additional remark, saying: "Crimes solved subsequently in 1992." Can you tell us what that is?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On-site investigations were carried out. Criminal reports were filed. Work continued on shedding more light on the crimes committed. When more information is compiled, then results are achieved. So that is what is listed here, what the results achieved were, in terms of finding the perpetrators, solving the cases, and so on, which shows that the cases were live, as we say in police jargon. They were still being worked on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there are no objections, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm still not altogether clear. Is this a photocopy of parts of the register, or is it a specially produced document? That's what I'm not clear on at the moment. It is a document, according to the list that was given to the Defence, by Mr. Bjelosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thought that you had provided sufficient information, but could you please explain what kind of document this is and on the basis of what it was compiled, for what needs.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that this is an extract from the register where criminal reports are registered, as well as crimes that had been committed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry, that is still not an answer to the question. What I'm asking is: Is this a photocopy of the actual entry as it appears in the registers, or is it a specially typed up document, by this witness or someone else, containing copies, if you like, or extracts from the register. That's all I want to know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you answer that question?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are extracts from the register. This extract was used for compiling an analysis for a meeting, for analysing the information related to the documents from -- or to the incidents from that period. I don't know whether that will do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I please show the next document and then we'll go back to this one. I believe that it will be clearer then. Can we look at 1D358. That is tab 245.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have page 2, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, please have a look at the monitor. Perhaps you can see it better. I think that it's better than the photocopy that you have. Are you familiar with this document? And could you please explain what this is.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the register, the criminal register. And this is the prescribed form where records are kept of the crimes that had been committed, the files -- the reports that had been filed and so on. The extract that we referred to a moment ago was compiled on the basis of this register.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let us clarify something for the transcript. What was the abbreviated -- what was the abbreviation used for this register?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: KU. Or K Upisnik; K register.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Please have a look at page 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us have that shown on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, could you please explain this page 5. What is contained in this form of the K register? And could you finally give us your comments with regard to the writing in red. If you would like to have something zoomed in, please tell us, and we'll have it done.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said a moment ago, that is the form. The date of entry is there, and the date when the entry is made, then who the injured parties are, who the perpetrators are. And this is kept throughout the year. At the end of a calendar year, it is concluded for that year, and that was, indeed, done here, and that is what it says in red handwriting. So for 1992, it says, "Up until number 37, including number 37," and then it goes on, in cycles.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: These numbers, the consecutive numbers that appear there in the first column, do these numbers have anything to do with the numbers that we saw on some criminal reports on, say, the criminal reports we looked at a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. We saw that on every one of the criminal reports there were numbers that said "KU" and a particular number. So that is that number and it would be handwritten on each and every document. Then that copy would be archived, and the number is identical.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On this page, the date of the last entry is which date? If you can see ...

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I can see it correctly, I think it's the 30th of December. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please go back to page 2. Let us just see what the date of the first entry was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 2nd of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The injured party, under number 1, is?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hidic Sajda [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What is the ethnicity of the lady who is the injured party?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: An ethnic Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bjelosevic, could you please tell us now how, on the basis of this document, if I understood you correctly you said that, that the previous document was compiled on the basis of this document. Can you explain this to us? How was the previous document created?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was created by taking information from this K register. And then, if you collate the two, you will see that it is an exact reflection of that. This is a survey that was made on the basis of this K register. It clearly shows that that is the information that was extracted from here, and the persons who were the injured parties are exactly those that are described in the criminal reports. Also, as far as perpetrators are concerned, it is exactly what was stated in those documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, can I say straight away, that subject to simply the witness saying when this document was prepared, I withdraw my objection. It came up originally, if we go back, because the English translation refers to something called the KP book. And for the life for me, I didn't know what the KP book -- and now we can see it is a mistyping of some kind or another. So subject to the witness simply saying when this document was produced, I have no further objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And who did it and for what purpose.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Exactly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is precisely what I wanted to ask you now. For which purposes was this document compiled, if you know? Who compiled it? 389D1, tab 215, is the document I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the date with any degree of reliability. However, it was drafted for an analysis, an analysis of crimes which had been perpetrated, the injured parties, the perpetrators and so on and so forth. I really can't remember the date when this was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember the year when this was drafted and who the author of the document was?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The author of the document could have been exclusively somebody who was in charge of maintaining the records because nobody else had access to those records. Who precisely among them drafted this document, I don't know. But it was one of the staff members who were in charge of the register, who were recording crimes in the register, and it is obvious that an analysis had to be done, and that in preparation for the meeting at which the analysis would be carried out, the documents were prepared.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And can you explain to us how was it regulated in practical terms? You say that somebody was in charge of the records and the register. Can you please be more precise and can you give us any of the names, the names of people who in 1992 had access to those documents.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a -- an office or a desk officer who worked with the register. It was part of that person's job description to maintain the register. And the same thing is true today. I don't remember who it was who was in charge of that office or who the desk officer was. It was a long time ago. I don't remember really.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you say "this register," do you mean the KU register or something else?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I mean the KU register. Somebody who was in charge of maintaining the KU register, the criminal register.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Was it just one person who was authorised in the Security Services Centre to make entries into the register?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that there were two people. Maybe initially there was just one, and later, I believe that two persons had that authority. And as the crime department expanded, the number of personnel increased, but initially there was just one person.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know, Your Honours, whether you're satisfied with this answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, it's about the third time of asking but he still hasn't answer the question, asked again by Mr. Zecevic. At least which year was this document brought into existence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't say with any degree of reliability. But it certainly wasn't done in 1992, because we can see that everything that happened in 1992 is contained herein.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, since all this data can be found in the KU register anyway, in order to save time I will withdraw my proposal. I thought that this might be a better overview. Maybe it would be easier for us to have an overview on two pages rather than to go through the entire register. However, since the witness is not in a position to assist us any further, I will withdraw my proposal to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, before you go that far, there is a question, the answer to which I'm curious about, and I'm going to ask the question bluntly. Was it prepared for the -- Mr. Bjelosevic, was this summary or - that's my word - prepared for the purpose of proceedings before this Tribunal? Or was it for some internal purpose in -- in the country of origin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was prepared for the purpose of proceedings, or perhaps to prepare for a future analysis of crimes. I don't know. It -- it's all possible. It -- in any case, the document is identical to the contents of the KU register. When this document was drafted, what was its purpose? I really can't remember, as I sit here today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: In which case, Mr. Zecevic, perhaps we better leave it with your withdrawal of your attempt to exhibit it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, can you remind us of the tab number of that document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Document tab number is 215, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So I'm withdrawing this -- the offer of this document to be admitted. As I said already, this is already contained in the previous documents and 1D358.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bjelosevic, according to what you know, the KU register that we have just had a look at, was it regularly maintained at the Doboj Security Services Centre?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From the moment the Doboj Security Services Centre was assigned its elements in 1992, as of that time, that register was regularly kept.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I believe that you mentioned a month as well.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mid-July, or, rather, the month of July 1992. I believe that is rather precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We saw just a moment ago a certain number underlined at the end of the year. Do you remember the number?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was 37. I don't know if that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain the significance of the number, 37, in the KU register for the year 1992?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means that the Security Services Centre, the crime department, pursued that many cases that pertained to its authority. That's how many cases were pursued and entered into the KU register. I would like to say that public security stations dealt with crimes that pertained to their own authority, and they also were duty-bound to maintain their own KU registers.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In other words, would you say that all public security stations, the ones in the territory of your Security Services Centre, have that same duty? Were they duty-bound to maintain KU registers or not?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were. They were duty-bound to do that. There are other records maintained by public security stations, but since we're talking about the KU register, I would like to say that that record was mandatory and they also had to keep a record of daily evidence -- events and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You were talking about the authorities of the Security Services Centre and the public security stations. What did you mean by that? Just briefly.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, Security Services Centres dealt with crimes for which a higher court was authorised; whereas, public security stations were -- dealt with crimes that were under the authority of basic courts. So when we're talking about some more complicated and aggravated crimes, it was the Security Services Centre that was in charge of investigating and pursuing those crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you say "Security Services Centre," was the abbreviation CSB?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the abbreviation, CSB.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And when you mention public security stations, their abbreviation was SJB.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The first letters of each of the three words, SJB.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at 261D1, tab 181.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is a dispatch sent by the Security Services Centre Doboj on the 23rd of November. In the left-hand side corner, there is your name typed up. Can you tell us whether you're familiar with this document, whether you sent this document, and what is its background?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember the document because we had a problem. I have already said that a number of stations, or, rather, the buildings where the public security stations were housed had been torched or destroyed during combat. And we did not have proper forms for each of the stations. However, our public security stations received instructions or, rather, their chiefs of Crime Prevention Departments were instructed to use provisional notebooks. And here we are addressing the MUP and requesting a certain number of proper forms so that they could be used for keeping records, and everything that was provisionally recorded was going to be copied into proper forms. This was a problem for Derventa, Modrica, Brod, and for those public security stations that were in the part of the territory around Maglaj, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What particular form does this dispatch relate to, Mr. Bjelosevic?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The KU register, the one that we saw just a while ago. The crime register. We just had the -- that register on -- both on the monitor and in my documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unless there are objections, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D493, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bjelosevic, let us briefly go back to the register, the KU -- or the crime register which you saw just a while ago. On two occasions, we looked at it, and we saw that there were 37 entries for the year 1992. Do you have any information to the effect that all crimes were entered which were within your authority during the period that we already spoke about?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All crimes which were either reported to us or were detected by police officers, all those crimes were registered, and they were entered in the crime register.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We saw in the previous document that some public security stations faced problems with proper forms or -- or the lack thereof. Did the same problem exist in the Doboj Security Services Centre?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During that period, we had forms that we can see here, and that was done properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One more document before we take our next break. Can the witness please be shown P1893, tab 102.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is a Prosecutor's document which the Prosecutor tendered in evidence. The date is 2nd of September, 1992. This is a cover letter, as it were, drafted by the Security Services Centre. Your name is typed up. The document has been signed. There is a stamp. Are you familiar with the document? What is it about?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the document was drafted by the Security Services Centre in Doboj. This is a cover letter, and the document is an activity report covering the period from the 24th of August to the 31st of August, 1992. This activity report --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let us see page number 2, then.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The activity report shows what the Crime Prevention Department did during that week. And in the second paragraph, towards the end of it, you can see that the -- in each specific case, we established the elements and so on and so forth. Which means that there had been a meeting. What follows is the activities that were taken with this record. There is the structure of all the crimes that were committed, and then a breakdown by crimes, the total number of crimes committed by known perpetrators, by unknown perpetrators, and so on and so forth. And then there is reference to the things that were within the purview of uniformed police that pertain to the disruptions of law and order, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just briefly, let us explain. This report issued by the Security Services Centre was sent, as we saw on the first page, to the Ministry of the Interior. Would you say that this report encompasses all public security stations, including the Security Services Centre in Doboj or not?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does, all of them. You can see that from the text itself, from the description. Because they list what happened in each of the municipalities covered by the station.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And this is a weekly report. It covers the period of one week.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a weekly report, and my signature is both on the covering letter and the document itself, the report itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
