utterances.text: Let us just clarify one more thing. When it says "(a), crime," it means that there were 48 criminal offences committed, out of which 37 by unknown perpetrators.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Now let us take a look at 214D1, tab 103. Take a look at the second page. You will find your name typed there, as well as a stamp and a signature. This document comes from the Security Services Centre in Doboj. The date is the 4th of September, 1992, and it is addressed to the Ministry of the Interior, Crime Prevention Administration. Is this your document; and what is it about?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document originating from the Security Services Centre in Doboj. We can all see the date. And this is a monthly report. It covers the period between the 1st of August and the 31st of August, 1992. I signed this document, and it shows the structure and the number of criminal offences, and you also have the breakdown regarding the municipalities. On the first page we see a handwritten note, "V. Pero." This is Petar Vujicic. He was the head of the analytical department. So obviously this is a copy that ended up in the analytical department.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Analytical department of?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of the Ministry of the Interior, at the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I see what the time is. I have one or two more questions related to this document. Should I pose those questions after the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: If they're short questions, let's deal with it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, bearing in mind this document, and bearing in mind your recollections, could you tell us what was the most frequent kind of criminal offences committed in this period?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The most frequent criminal offences were offences against property. By far. This is a characteristic of that period. You have to bear in mind the general situation. There were thousands and thousands of refugees. They were looking for accommodation for themselves and their families, and this was especially true when people started returning to their houses which have been destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In this document - just a second - the fifth paragraph, you refer to analysis. Do you maybe remember what this is about?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you be brief, please.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll be brief. There was an order issued by Minister Stanisic. He requested an analysis to be submitted to the Ministry of the Interior that would contain, among other things, elements of war crimes, if any. And this paragraph simply refers to the fact that we made this analysis and that certain inspectors visited our headquarters, and they controlled our work in this regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there is no objection, I would like to tender the document. [In English] I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D494, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Now I see the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we take the break and resume in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: May I continue, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. [Interpretation] Can we have the following document, 226D1, tab 124.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, on the second page of this document, at the bottom, we see your name typed, Chief of Centre, Andrija Bjelosevic, as well as your signature. The document originates from the Security Services Centre in Doboj, and it is addressed to the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska, and the administrations are listed. First of all, can you confirm that this is your document; and then can you explain it.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This document originates from the Security Services Centre in Doboj. The date we can all see. It's a weekly report that was sent to the Ministry of the Interior. More specifically, police administration and the prevention -- Crime Prevention Administration. It bears my signature. This report refers to two lines of work, as you can see: The crime and the police affairs. And then you see the breakdown, known perpetrators, unknown perpetrators and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you briefly comment on (a), crime; can you confirm the numbers, total crimes committed, known and unknown perpetrators; and can you also explain the comment given in the last sentence?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The total number of crimes committed is 51; known perpetrators, 10; unknown perpetrators, 41. You can see, again, that most of them are crimes against property. 29 thefts; 8 aggravated thefts, et cetera. So you can see that most of them are crimes against property.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, does this report cover all the public security stations and the CSB in Doboj?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a cumulative report that contains all the data pertaining to the areas of all the stations and the centre itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you comment on something on the second page. If we take a look at the first paragraph, and then we see various dash points listing measures and activities undertaken by the employees of the MUP. I'm interested in the fifth bullet point, where it says: "Seven reports were submitted to the prosecutor's office (Doboj)." What is this all about?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This relates to criminal offences and the criminal reports. So these are the acts that were subject of criminal reports and that are now already being processed by the prosecutor offices.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there is no objection, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D495, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tab 130, 232D1.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The date of the document is the 24th of September, 1992. On the second page, we find the signature and the stamp. And on the first page, we see some handwritten comments.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is also a document originating from the Security Services Centre in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Just a second. I have to check something.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour. We received one copy of this document from the Prosecution, so we uploaded this copy into the e-court -- or, no, the other way around. The copy that I have here is the copy that we received from the Prosecution, and what we see in e-court is our copy. My copy bears number 0360-8239; that's ERN number. And the following page is 240. My copy bears both the stamp and the signature, and it also has some handwritten note on the first page. In order not to complicate things, since the documents are identical, maybe it would be best if the witness commented on the document that we see on the screens, because we are interested in its contents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, please, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bjelosevic, tell us whether this is your document, and could you please explain it.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the first page on the screen now. Yes, this is a document originating from the Security Services Centre in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you want to see the second page so that you can take a look at the signature?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, please. All right. It's my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now go back to the first page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a weekly report that was sent to the Ministry of the Interior, more specifically, to the Police Affairs Administration and the Crime Prevention Administration. It covers the period between the 13th and the 20th September, 1992. Again, it covers both crime and police affairs. If you take a look at the breakdown of criminal offences, you will see that the total number of crimes committed is 68. However, now, it's 46 by known perpetrators and 22 by unknown perpetrators. This reflects a progress in discovery of perpetrators. Still, the list is dominated by crimes against property. 60 thefts, three aggravated thefts. You can also see the number of on-site investigations that were conducted. Can we have now the next page?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you first explain, or, rather, give us your opinion, what is the reason for the difference that we can observe here, the difference between known and unknown perpetrators? I'm referring to the fact that the number of known perpetrators is higher here.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whenever there is a significant increase in the percentage of perpetrators who were discovered, it means that the police was doing their job well. Of course, it could also be circumstances that work to the effect that a higher number of perpetrators were discovered. But I can tell you that, as time went on, the work was more serious, more thorough. Evidence was gathered, and all this enabled the increase in the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there is no objection, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D496, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, if I might return to a suggestion made by Judge Harhoff earlier today, is there a possibility of a batch of these like documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I only -- I only admitted three documents, the reports, and I only wanted to show the increase of the known perpetrators versus unknown perpetrators, and that's the last report that I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I see. I see. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document is 18D1, tab 68A.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, I didn't hear the number, the tab number.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The tab number is 68A. Are you familiar with this document and can you comment on it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the daily event bulletin containing information from the territory of the Security Services Centre in Doboj. This report covers the situation at the battlefield, saying that a part of the Derventa municipality, Bijelo Brdo, and the Bosanski Brod municipality are places where fighting is still going on, and there are still some enemy strongholds remaining. It also says that enemy forces are still operating from Tesanj, and then it gives the assessment of the danger, and so on and so forth. So here we can see information taped in the informative bulletin from the Security Services Centre in Doboj. When the communications lines were working, this was regularly sent to the Ministry of the Interior to be included in their informative bulletin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This handwritten comment that we can see at the top of the page, do you maybe recognise the handwriting?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recognise the handwriting. It says, "Daily report number 69, 18 July," and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In the second paragraph, it talks about the robberies being committed in Derventa, Modrica and Odzak; in other words, the recently liberated territories.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Is this information in any way related to the reports that we were looking at a moment ago? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those numbers contain this information. And I have to emphasise that the territories of those municipalities were the territories with very difficult situation. And when those territories were liberated, people went back to their property only to find it destroyed, plundered, and burned down. They tried to recover whatever they could, which then led to an increase in robberies and crimes against property.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Please just give me a comment on the last sentence in that second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In relation to documentation.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When the police, or the milicija, as it was known at the time, would try to prevent this plunder, very often people based aggressively, and they drew weapons. These cases were documented. And may I also add that what happened was that in some cases that were all too frequent, when people in uniform, the military, were transporting certain goods in cars, and when the police would stop them, then they would show permits given to them by their commands, allowing them to take some goods for themselves. Wherever possible, I tried to obtain telefaxes so when there was electricity, then we could photocopy those permits and document the fact that goods were being taken away that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there are no objections, I would like to tender this document into evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D497.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I just ask if he knows whose writing that is at the top? If you look at the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I asked, and he said he doesn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh, I see. I'm sorry, I missed that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And this is the document we received ... [Interpretation] The next document is 651D1, tab 137.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, let us look at page 2. Could you please give us your comment as to whether are you familiar with this document and whether you know what this is all about.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a document from the municipality of Samac. It was signed by the president of the War Presidency, Dr. Blagoje Simic. You can see that it has to do with providing consent for the participation of volunteers from Serbia in a certain operation directed at Orasje.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can we please have page 1. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to recall another thing. The municipality of Samac, or, rather, their War Presidency, had a bit of a claim on the municipality of Odzak as well, invoking some kind of referendum of certain local communes. However, since there was a military administration in place, there was quite a bit of misunderstanding between the military command and the War Presidency of Samac. In Article 5 of this decision, you can see that permission is being given for members of this volunteer unit to gain possession of certain items. And it says: "Passenger cars, technical goods, clothing," and so on. This just confirms what I have been trying to say time and again in order for Their Honours to try to understand what the situation was at the time. It was a state of true chaos where powers were entwined, Crisis Staffs tried to retain some of their powers through the War Presidencies, and it was exceptionally, exceptionally difficult to work in a lawful manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What is the date of this document?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "At a session held on 4th of October, 1992," et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there are no objections, I would like to tender this document as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Before we get that far, could I just ask about the -- the underlying work or the underlying structure of this, which is a bit unclear to me. The War Presidency is requesting authorisation to allow volunteers to take part in a military operation against -- or in the territory of Orasje. Now, who is the addressee of this? Mr. Witness, can you help us out here? What is the underlying work method here? What's happening here in this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As you can see, I don't know what the translation is, but this decision does allow, allow - that is what it literally says - the civilian authorities of the municipality of Samac are allowing this, an agreement with the relevant commands of the army. They don't say which one. They say that what is allowed is the participation of volunteers in the operation directed at Orasje. Article 5 of this decision says: "While carrying out the operation to free the territory of Orasje municipality," it says in capital letters, "every member of the Serbian volunteer unit is hereby ALLOWED," in capital letters, "to gain possession of items seized from the enemy," et cetera. So they are not asking for permission or consent. They are allowing them to do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you for this clarification, but it raises to me at least two questions. One is: Why would the civilian authority be entitled to allow volunteers to be put under the command of the army? That's my first question. My second question is: Why would the civilian authority of the Crisis Staff, as it is, allow volunteers to commit crimes? To seize property illegally. Let's take my two questions one at a time. First of all, what is the relation between the Crisis Staff and [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, I did understand the question. I did understand the question. It is quite clear. But I don't know the answer to that question myself. Believe me. I find that completely -- well, let me allow myself to say this. It goes beyond the law, and it goes beyond reason, if you can put it that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But was it the normal way of proceeding in instances where volunteers were put under the command of -- of the -- of the army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. This is -- this is the War Presidency assuming powers that are far too great. Your Honours, in order to clarify the situation for you to see what it was actually like, may I say that I, with my co-workers, went to the municipality of Samac after the inspectors of the CSB Doboj visited the public security station of Samac and inspected their mode of work, and, in the process, discovered a great many irregularities. I knew that Chief Todorovic had been appointed by the Crisis Staff sometime in April 1992, of course, without any kind of consultations with the centre or any consent coming from the centre. Then I went with my co-workers to try to reach agreement with them, to have that man replaced from that position, because work was not being carried out properly. What I experienced then was a most unpleasant situation. It came precisely from Mr. Simic. He reacted very arrogantly to what I had set out to say. He said to me, "Where were you in April when we had fierce clashes with the enemy here? We appointed Todorovic, and he is going to be the chief of the public security station." And he also put a question to me, asking me what my inspectors were doing in the municipality of Odzak. He told me to be careful, saying that I could fare worse than in Teslic. After those words, I asked my co-workers to go back to Doboj with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And for the second question that I put to you, the authorisation to loot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, no reasonable person can understand that. I truly cannot understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Back to you, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The document is admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D498, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I was of impression that, Your Honour, Judge Delvoie, wanted to -- no. I'm sorry. [Interpretation] Your Honours, now I have a number of documents that are documents that deal with identical questions. The documents themselves are not identical in form, but they are all a type of approval or permit given by certain military commanders to soldiers to carry certain goods out of territories where war operations were under way. I have a total of 11 such documents confirming this. I don't know how the Trial Chamber wishes me to proceed. I would now like to show the witness one of these documents, if the Trial Chamber agrees, and if the Prosecutor agrees, so that we can hear the witness's comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So please proceed as you have indicated, Mr. Zecevic. You could begin with one or two, and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours. [Interpretation] 548D1, tab 78, is the number of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, this is a certificate from Tactical Group 3. Colonel Slavko Lisica is the signatory. Are you familiar with this document; and what can you tell us about it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm familiar with the document. This is a document that the police at the check-point took from the person who drove those things that are listed in here. However, I would like to offer a short comment, if I may. There's a drastic difference between this and what the War Presidency of Samac municipality approved. As you can see from the wording of the certificate, the person in question was a combatant who fled from Western Slavonia, who lost everything there. In order to be able to join the army as a combatant, and there are other such cases that I'm familiar with, in order for him to be a member of the unit and to fight, he has to have some bare essentials for his family. And here you see what the command approves for him to take home. Where the things came from, I really don't know. However, the command did issue a certificate allowing him to drive all that and to secure relatively good living conditions for his family. I don't know whether this was taken from houses or from some storages, I don't know. But it is very clear what the certificate refers to.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It seems to me that you said at the very beginning - I don't know if I understood you properly - you say that the police at the check-point took this document. Did the police take the document or -- I believe that you mentioned copy machine and fax machine at the check-points. I don't know whether the document was copied or taken from the person.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some documents were taken, and their originals remained in the centre, and a certain number was copied, where conditions were in place for a fax machine to be used. There were no photocopiers at the time. When there was electricity we made photocopies. I remember that there are documents in their original form as well as in copies.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, since all these documents actually illustrate the point, I would like to tender just one document in order not to burden the case file with an excessive number of documents. I would like to tender perhaps this one and maybe another one after this. Unless there are objections by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, firstly, Mr. Zecevic said to him, "I believe you mentioned photocopying or fax facilities at the check-points." I saw no such assertion by the witness. But for the moment I'd like to know, if I may, and this, of course, is difficult because of the so-called author, where this document actually was obtained by the Defence from? It doesn't appear to come from Colonel Lisica's book. And it's not on their list of ones provided by Bjelosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Korner, we provided you with a list of the provenance of the documents. This is a document which we received from the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. That's why I asked. It's not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'm -- you will have to deal with Ms. Savic about that. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I'm sorry. If I understand there is an error - I'm delighted to see that even Ms. Savic can make errors from time to time - that's fine. As regards the suggestion that this should be put in and none of the others, Your Honours, I think it's a matter for Your Honours. I'm not taking any point.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And the second thing, Your Honours, page 58, 13, these cases were documented and may I also -- it starts at line 8: "These cases were documented. And may I also add that what happened was that in some cases that were all too frequent, when people in uniform, the military, were transporting certain goods in cars, and when the police would stop them, then they would show permits given to them by their commands, allowing them to take some goods for themselves. Wherever possible, I tried to obtain telefaxes so when there was electricity, then we could photocopy those permits and documents. The fact that good -- and document the fact that goods were being taken away that way." That was the reference. So it's --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: -- page 58. So I don't know where we are now, whether there was an opposition ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, so we'll take this one. And you say you have another one to put in. Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this document, 65 ter 5481, will become Exhibit 1D499.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 549D1 is the following document I would like to look at with you. That's tab 79. The following document in that sequence. This again is a document signed by -- or, rather, Colonel Slavko Lisica's name is typed up. I don't know whether the signature is his. And the document bears the date 3rd August 1992. Can you tell us something about the document?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is another of the documents whereby people are allowed to be assisted -- to fallen or injured -- or, rather, people are allowed to transport certain things and there's a list of those things that people can transport. Those are usually household essentials. Again, this was checked at the check-point and documented. And so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unless there are objections, I would like to tender this document as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D500, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, would you have another one that is not signed by Colonel Lisica but by somebody else?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I said, Your Honours, I have 11 so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Unless they're all from Colonel Lisica.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no, they are not. They are not. I will show another --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Another unit, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Another unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. [Interpretation] 531D1, tab 146.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is a document which was signed by the Municipal Defence Commander KIK, which probably stands for Captain First Class, Pero Stojakovic. The date I believe is the 9th October 1992. The name is typed up. I'm not sure about the signature. Can you comment upon this document?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This document was issued by the command of the Municipal Defence of Derventa. It is entitled as "Approval." Kalenderovci local commune is granted approval to transport machinery, as listed in this document. Captain First Class Pero Stojakovic signed this document. He was the commander of the Municipal Defence Command, and the institution in question is the craftsmen guild, who were supposed to organise work in Derventa if they received the machinery. I don't know where the machinery was from, but I'm familiar with the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Is this one of the documents that was found at a check-point by the police?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was found at a police check-point.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: May I have this document exhibited also?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes. Who is the beneficiary of this approval?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness can answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The local commune, the Kalenderovci local commune, as can you see it here. And the machinery was intended for the association of craftsmen or small businesses, the craftsmen guild. That association was supposed to safe-guard the machinery, first of all, and later on, if they needed the machinery, if the machinery was assigned to them, they could use that machinery to organise their own production. If you look at the first paragraph, you will see that it says here: "Approval is hereby granted to the Kalenderovci local commune, Gornji Detlak branch, to remove the following machinery in order to protect it, and later, should it be assigned to them for the formation of a craftsmen's guild." In other words, initially they were they were supposed to safe-guard it and in a later stage, if possible, the machinery could also be used for their production. I believe that sometime later the machinery was returned to the factory from which it -- it had originally been removed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you for this clarification. I guess my question was -- or my concern was that in the previous documents that Counsel Zecevic showed to us, it was Colonel Lisica who authorised a combatant under his command to seize war booty, which makes sense, because obviously the colonel would have had jurisdiction over the soldier. But here it's different. Here is another officer of the army who is authorising a local commune to seize property. But let's just take it at face value and not spend any more time on this. But it's an interesting mix of powers back and forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we'll admit this and mark this document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D501, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown 278D1, which is at tab 199. Can we look at the second page of the document. The typed-up signature is that of Andrija Bjelosevic, the chief of centre. However, there is also the word "za," or "for," and somebody's signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you please comment upon this document, Mr. Bjelosevic. What is this document about? What kind of information is provided? What is this document?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is information that was submitted to the Ministry of the Interior to the Crime Prevention Department at the ministry's request, because you can see a link between their dispatch dated the 30th of November, 1992. Certain information is provided to the ministry. The document was signed by Mirko Stojcinovic, the chief of the public security centre in the services -- Security Services Centre of Doboj. And I'm familiar with this document. The document was drafted at the administration's request.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you please clarify the numbers. For example, at the very beginning, the number of dead persons, what period does the figure, this one and all the other ones in the document, refer to?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose that this was -- for the period ending with the 30th of November, 1992. Information was requested about the number of dead, the structure of those dead persons, how many were civilians, how many were military, how many members of the service there were, and when it says "the service" what is meant is the MUP, men, women, and so on and so forth. So this is the information that was available to us at the time. The total number of dead was provided for the period ending in -- on the 30th of November, 1992. It is possible that the figures relate to some other period, but we would have to locate the relevant dispatch, and there you will find a clear instruction.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Besides providing the number of persons, this document also provides some other facts. Am I right? This document also provides some other facts. Not only just the number of persons and the number of crimes; right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's a reference to destroyed and damaged buildings, both privately owned and socially owned.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you please have a look and tell us whether there is any reference to places of worship? I think that it is the first tab after material damage from the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the first page?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, on the first page.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume that it has all been included, but I really do not seem to be able to find it right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It says: "In order to establish the material damage sustained by material ..."

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes, yes. Everything is referred to. 12 sabotages, six of which were bridges, four religious buildings, and two against railway -- railroads. And then it says in parentheses: "Information received from," et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: At any rate, this document was sent by your chief of public security sector to the MUP of Republika Srpska to the department for crime prevention in Bijeljina. Was it sent with your knowledge and with your approval?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know when this information was being collected I was probably somewhere out in the field, and Chief Stojcinovic signed it, which was quite all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there are no objections, I would like to move for this document to be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D502, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document I would like to show you is 203D1, tab 81.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just one intervention in the transcript, Your Honours. Page 71, line 11, should be my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, this is a document dated the 3rd of August, I believe, 1992. What is typewritten towards the bottom of the page is Chief of the Centre, Andrija Bjelosevic. Can you tell us whether this is, indeed, your document, whether you're familiar with it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a document from the CSB Doboj, and it was sent to the public security stations in the territory of the centre. This document is based on a meeting held in the Ministry of the Interior and the documents -- and the positions that were taken then. And what was agreed upon at that meeting, or the collegium, what was asked for by the minister, what his instructions were, and I'm dealing with this on the ground. I'm saying what should be done in the future with regard to reinforcing the service. And I say that a document is being drafted, rules on the internal staffing of the MUP, and then there are further suggestions as to how new personnel should be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did you sign this document?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a document that I signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there are no objections, I would like to tender this document as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D503, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I think it should be 504. Because previous one was 503. I'm sorry. I am a bit confused. [Interpretation] Another document. The date is the same. 20481 -- 204D1, tab 82.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this document is also dated the 3rd of August, 1992, submitted to all public security stations, to the chief, signed by Andrija Bjelosevic, chief of the centre. Can you confirm whether this is a document of yours and whether you remember what it pertains to; and can you explain to us what this was about?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document is from the CSB Doboj. The date is the one stated. And the signature at the end of the document is mine. This was sent to all the public security stations in the territory of the centre. Certain information is being requested. Information that has to do with the functioning of administrative matters. It has to do with personal documents and related issues. As you can see, personal identification cards, personal names, registration of permanent and temporary residence, citizenship, official registers, personal identification numbers, registration of motor vehicles, procuring, owning and carrying weapons and ammunition, refugees, issuing personal documents to refugees, state border crossing control, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, did you have any problems with the records pertaining to these documents, or is this about something else?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had problems with possession of these forms, especially in the area of Derventa, Modrica, Brod, Odzak later. Because in Derventa, Brod and Modrica, buildings had burned down, buildings where the public security stations were, so documentation was destroyed and the actual forms as well. I would like to note that these forms, already in the beginning of April, when the self-styled territorials took over the station of Derventa, on that occasion, all these forms were simply taken away. That was the objective, actually, to record all the problems involved and to submit that to the MUP. We discussed that problem at the collegium meeting of the 11th of June, and what followed was a document, a letter from the ministry, along those lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there are no objections, I would like to tender this document as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: What do you intend to show with this document, Mr. Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, what I intend to show is that, on the 11th of July, there was a collegium, the first collegium. One of the matters discussed was this particular issue, the problem with the administrative matters which the MUP is also working as a part of their duties in accordance with the law, and also the problem of misappropriation of these forms which are specific forms and which have been stolen or burned or -- and the -- the possibility of misuse of these -- or forgery of these documents. And as witness acknowledged, there was also one -- one order sent from the MUP in that respect, and this is showing that the CSB is following the order from the MUP and from -- and the conclusion decided upon on the 11th of July, they are actually performing their duty and sending this request to their SJBs in the territory. That is the reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But, surely, that would not be a surprise, would it? That a CSB is following orders from the MUP on civilian and administrative matters?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, this is to illustrate that the CSBs were performing the duties of -- agreed upon on the 11th of July collegium. And I think it's very relevant. Not only this, this is showing them -- the administrative matters, but also all other aspects of the conclusions reached on the 11th of July collegium meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D504, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I see the time, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Bjelosevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we take the adjournment for today, to resume in this courtroom tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 19th day of April, 2011, at 9.00 a.m.
